analysis.title: Privacy: the missing layer of institutional finance
key_insights: Privacy coins are the only part of the crypto market trading above last year's peak. Per 21shares, privacy coins stood 236% since Bitcoin's October 2025 peak, while the average crypto asset excluding stablecoins fell 26%.

On 28 October the DTCC launched its tokenisation service on the Canton Network, a blockchain where each participant sees only its own transactions. Twenty institutions including JPMorgan, Citi and Morgan Stanley have signed up, per CoinDesk.

Public blockchains expose every balance and transfer, which institutions cannot accept. The report separates anonymity (hidden from everyone, regulators included) from confidentiality (hidden from the public, visible to authorised parties through viewing keys). Institutional use depends on the second.
21shares values the privacy sector at about $35bn, of which Zcash is about $24bn. That is about 1.4% of the crypto market excluding stablecoins.
28% of circulating ZEC sits in shielded pools, up from 9% in 2023 per 21shares. Coins moved into the pools tend to stay there.
Grayscale launched the first US-listed spot Zcash ETF in August. It had more than $750mn in assets by late October.
McKinsey expects tokenised financial assets excluding cryptocurrencies and stablecoins to reach about $2tn by 2030 in its base case and up to $4tn in an optimistic scenario.

Exposure comes through three channels: dedicated privacy coins (Zcash, Monero), institutional infrastructure (Canton and Canton Coin), and generalist blockchains (Ethereum, Solana, NEAR) with confidential transactions on their roadmaps.

Broadridge's repo platform processes more than $8tn a month on Canton per Blockworks Research. Most of that is repeatedly counted repo lending. Tokenised assets actually held on the network are about $367bn per RWA.xyz.

Canton Coin holders capture only a small part of network activity, through fees banks pay. Banks have no need to hold CC beyond paying fees, so the link between adoption and token value is the weakest in this segment.

Zcash's optional privacy with viewing keys sits closer to what regulators can accept than Monero's default anonymity. Usage benefits ZEC directly because users must hold it. European rules do not currently make that distinction.

From July 2027 the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation will prohibit crypto-asset service providers from handling anonymity-enhancing coins, likely pushing exchanges serving European clients to delist Monero and Zcash ahead of the deadline.
Exchange access is already limited. OKX removed Monero and Zcash and Binance removed Monero for trading since 2024.
Market risks: Zcash is about two thirds of sector value, and volatility is extreme. ZEC fell from a late-September high near $1,680 to about $1,050 by mid-October per Crypto Briefing.

Technical risk: in May 2026 a researcher found a flaw in Zcash's main shielded pool, present since 2022, that could in theory have allowed undetected counterfeit coins. ZEC fell 38% after disclosure per Decrypt, and a new pool was introduced in the July upgrade.
Conclusion: the sector is splitting between compliant privacy for institutions, which looks durable, and anonymous privacy for individuals, which faces tighter limits.

sector_views.rationale: Institutional confidentiality demand looks durable, but the report warns of regulatory limits on anonymous coins, extreme volatility, concentration in Zcash and weak token value accrual for Canton Coin.

crypto_views: Privacy coins were up 236% versus a 26% fall in the average non-stablecoin crypto asset since Bitcoin's October 2025 peak, per 21shares.
The DTCC launched tokenisation on Canton on 28 October. JPMorgan is bringing JPM Coin to the network and Broadridge runs its repo platform there.
Grayscale's spot Zcash ETF, launched in August, held more than $750mn by late October.
28% of ZEC supply is in shielded pools, up from 9% in 2023.
EU AMLR from July 2027 will bar crypto-asset service providers from handling anonymity-enhancing coins. Monero and Zcash delistings are likely on exchanges serving European clients.
Value accrual is a separate concern: institutional adoption of privacy infrastructure can grow while the associated tokens stagnate.
If Ethereum and Solana integrate privacy natively, dedicated projects could lose their premium.
risk_factors: EU AML Regulation from July 2027 and the FATF travel rule pressure exchanges to delist anonymity coins.
Concentration: Zcash is about two thirds of sector value.
Undetected bugs in zero-knowledge systems, as in the Zcash shielded pool flaw found in May 2026.
Token value may not capture institutional adoption, especially for Canton Coin.
Ethereum and Solana adding native privacy could erode the premium of dedicated projects.
Regulators could restrict onchain confidentiality as happened with Swiss banking secrecy.
vol_and_positioning: ZEC fell from a late-September high near $1,680 to about $1,050 by mid-October per Crypto Briefing.
ZEC fell 38% after the May 2026 disclosure of a flaw in its shielded pool, per Decrypt.
Zcash is about two thirds of the privacy sector's value, so the sector is concentrated.

tension_points.bull_case: Banks cannot move onchain without confidentiality. Canton is already used at scale, with JPMorgan, Broadridge and DTCC on the network, and 28% of ZEC sits in shielded pools.
tension_points.bear_case: EU rules from July 2027 will bar service providers from handling anonymity coins. Zcash is about two thirds of the sector, volatility is extreme, and institutional adoption may not lift the tokens.
tension_points.what_invalidates: DTCC volumes on Canton failing to pick up, Zcash's shielded share ceasing to rise, or strict EU enforcement in 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: Onchain privacy is becoming a prerequisite for institutional finance, but only in its confidential form.
theme_stances.evidence: Onchain privacy is becoming a prerequisite for institutional finance
